part1: Casting pentagrams — the whole colour system

Estelle teaches the casting of pentagrams: a five-pointed star drawn in one unbroken line with a spear of sunlight for a quill, then the circle, held in the mind over whatever you want to affect. She gives the full colour code — white protection, yellow-and-rose health, red passion, blue clarity, violet the higher realms, green living things, orange friendship — warns brown causes illness, and admits she casts small black pentagrams under Lady Jocelyn's lips at banquets so her words come out wrong.
And you would draw the five-pointed star first. And you do it in one line without lifting your quill.
Protective salt, and the thirteen-circle love spell

Asked for spells that could be used today, Estelle starts simple: salt across the doorway of your sleeping room while imagining it giving off light; salt sprinkled on the back of anyone whose intentions you doubt, while picturing a white wall, to confound their thoughts and tongue. Then the love working — under a waxing moon, pick a flower for yourself and one for the beloved, twine them, walk round them thirteen times asking for thirteen different intertwinings, bury them, and walk away without looking back.
That sounds like a love spell. It is.
The amulet purification ritual, and the planetary days

Amulet construction in detail — several symbols combined on one parchment, Jupiter for riches tempered with Apollo for craftsmanship, then sealed so the power can't dissipate. The purification never changes: the amulet ringed with ashes from the yew, salt sprinkled inside it in a five-pointed star, water set in the four directions, words spoken over it, then left to sit a number of days lucky for that amulet — six for money, five or seven for knowledge, three or nine for love.
you get the amulet and you surround it with a circle of ashes from the yew tree. And then within the circle, you sprinkle salt in the shape of a five-pointed star.
Making an amulet, and sealing it with a rainbow

The steps of making an amulet: decide its purpose, make the parchment with the right symbols, find a stone to give it power, fold the parchment round the stone, pouch it, and seal it with a ritual so the power concentrates instead of spreading over everything. The strongest sealing is done in the presence of an actual rainbow — otherwise at midnight in direct moonlight, on the day of the relevant deity. An amulet grows stronger the longer it is used and handed down.
And one very powerful way of sealing an amulet is with the use of a rainbow.
The druidess heals by drawing the fire

Aranaia describes being called to a sick person: a real fire built in a bowl and lit through the energy, gazed into purely as a focus, then drawn into themselves so the lady's power channels through their hands into the ill person while the prepared herbs work. She adds the purple and pink stones from the hills, worn strung over the point of light, which amplify what passes through her — each person finding her own stone by whether it repels, or radiates warmth like love.
And in drawing this fire into ourselves, we would draw the power. And then we would channel this energy into the person who was ill.
The elves — what each kind governs, and how to appease them

Estelle catalogues the little people as one family with branches: field elves who see that seed sprouts, ground elves in the mines, wood elves who warn game away from sport hunters and trip their horses, house elves in bright red who make bread rise and keep milk from curdling — and who reverse every bit of it when angered. To make peace you tear old clothes, throw ashes on your head, weep loudly, change into solemn dress, and leave broken bread with honey and milk in the corner they favour.
if you get them angry with you, your milk will start curdling, your cheese will stay runny, your bread will not rise
The initiation on the island, and how to channel energy

Candidates are robed in white and stood one at a time in the centre of the circle while the whole company presses focused energy at them — if it is repelled the body goes into spasms and the person is refused; if accepted they let it build and send it back by thought to the high priestess. Then the technique itself: hands over the solar plexus with fingers and thumbs together, opening yourself, breathing slowly and drawing more in with each breath, then palms out to let it flow like a stream.
The energy is pressed toward them to be either accepted or repelled.
The four festivals, and working the phases of the moon

Estelle names the sabbats — Hallowed Evening, Beltain, Llamas and the high festival — set as near the solstices and equinoxes as they can be, because the earth's energies flow a certain way then. At Llamas they invoke fire, stare into the flames and work on the land itself with their minds so the crops will grow. Hallowed Evening is the largest, with the herbal drinks, which can bring on prophecy and visions of ages hence.
however the energies are flowing through the earth is how they are flowing through you
The rainbow ritual that pierces the little people's protection

Estelle is with Grenell, an old wise woman, asking whether any ritual needs an actual rainbow present, since every colour has its own properties. Grenell teaches her rainbow meditation, and one ritual done in a rainbow's presence that lets you see through the spells of protection the little people and the unicorns cast over themselves — though not their children, who carry additional spells.
they are both magical peoples and they have their own spells of protection to where you can't see them unless you do this ritual
The monthly ceremony at the altar on the Isle of Mists

The women form a great circle around a black altar in the glade, carry candles round it and chant while focusing their love and essence onto a blazing clear stone set at its centre, which works as focuser and amplifier — the power returning to them greater than what they gave. The chant is not words but a sound like wind or waves; she begins to give it, then stops, saying it is not allowed.
It is a center of the focus. It is used as a focuser, also an amplifier.
Gem lore — and why a stone's magic has to be switched on

What Estelle has just learned about gems: red for the passions, pink for loyalty, green for friendship and growth, blue for the mind, purple for the spirit, black for truth-seeking and for initiating change. Clear stones, diamonds especially, are bad luck because they aren't oriented to any one vibration and attract good and bad alike. Dolores opens her eyes and shows her own turquoise pentacle ring, which Estelle reads as a good amulet.
you have to turn on the magic with your mind
The numbers, and herbs burned to evoke the goddess

Estelle argues the mass is full of stolen symbology and gives the numbers as her people hold them — the void before one, one as the source of energy, two for love spells, three active and multiplying, four stable, five the human body, six spiritual creation, seven its perfection, eight spiritual rest, nine three threes, ten the crowning. Then the fires built with herbs in them to colour the smoke and produce smells that evoke the goddess.
we often build fires and put herbs in the fires to make the smoke turn certain colors sometimes and to produce certain smells to help evoke the goddess
How Dolores herself was tested — scrying in a pot of water

Estelle reveals the test she had warned about. The group went to their sacred grove on a hilltop with its focusing stone, brought a pot filled with water, called down the guiding forces, presented Dolores to them and asked about her — and those who can read what appears in water gazed in and reported. They saw a black object that takes men's voices and gives them back, writing tools needing no ink pot, and a woman speaking from far down a long tunnel of time.
in the pot of water there are some of us who can read what is shown in the water
Shapes, pyramids, spinning widdershins, and the light

Triangles and pentagrams draw energy to a central focus point; the pyramid concentrates it so powerfully that a large one can do great damage, and crystal or pure stone works better than wood. Then the daily exercises — focusing on the light centre within until you can touch and hold it, and spinning widdershins on ground with earth power until the dizziness turns into feeling the energy. She finishes with surrounding yourself in light against dark spirits.
You move wintershins.
The unicorn, and its undisciplined magic

Unicorns are real physical animals hidden behind veils of protection cast by the little people. Estelle describes the one she saw at the edge of the woods: mother-of-pearl silver shot with rainbow colours, dark blue eyes, cloven hooves, a goat's beard, and a spiral horn as long as her leg with a line of silver in it, leaving a twinkling in the air as it ran. Humans cannot use its magic — you can ask its help, but it thinks like a unicorn.
It's undisciplined magic. It's always for good, but it's so undisciplined that you never can tell what form it's going to take.
What the old ways are — the goddess, the grove of thirteen oaks

Asked what the old ways mean, Estelle says they follow the cycles of the earth, that there are powers in the earth and moon through which the goddess reveals herself, and that working in harmony with them makes wondrous things happen. She names the grove of thirteen oaks she takes her lover to at night as a place of power that strengthens their bond each time, and explains the goddess has many names for her many faces.
It is a grove to the goddess. It is a group of 13 oak trees.
Karen reads two people's hands — the temple of light

Asked how her order recognises others of like training, Aranaia takes Harriet's hand in both of hers and reads it: a temple of light where many studied healing by vibrations they thought of as colours, and the doctrine that all healing must come from within. She then takes Dolores's hand, sees a great building of many books, throws the hand away in distress and says she saw fire.
You must not hope. You must believe. Hope has no power or strength.
Rank, the ageless high priestess, and paying for a healing

Aranaia is raised from lady-in-waiting to priestess and lays out the grades — maidens, ladies in waiting, priestesses, and the one high priestess, said to be ageless because the lady's hand is upon her. She reveals the law that a captured sister must kill herself or be killed by her own circle. Then, when her coughing continues, she explains it is not the pollen: she took part of a sick person's illness into her own body while healing.
When one takes and uses the energy to heal what is in this person, you take it upon yourself and I am just beginning to work it out.
Ley lines, power points, and witching with a willow rod

One line runs across the meadow where the giant's dance stands, at an intersection where earth power leaks from the centre; opening yourself at these points brings understanding and power. She describes finding them by witching with a rod cut from willow or fruit tree — held in the hands it tells you where the lines run, and the same method finds underground water, stone and metal if you focus on what you are seeking.
It is where the earth power leaks from the center.
Stonehenge raised by sound, built after the flood

Aranaia knows Stonehenge only as the giant's dance — a place of study for focusing powers and learning about the universe, built not by her people but by survivors of a land across the water that sank after its people angered the gods by misusing their abilities. The stones, it is told, were raised by music; the altar stone is lit by the fire of the sun at midsummer, which is the mystery.
it is said that it was raised by music. This is true. By using certain sounds, great weights can be lifted and moved.
Lenel, the sisters, and the wee folk who teach them

A second subject's entity, a young apprentice, tells how she was found: a wanderer who talked to the wee folk and was thought daffy, until one of the sisters who also befriended them took her in. She describes the knotted cord belt with its ornaments marking degrees of initiation, and refuses to explain them because she is sworn. Their work is healing and working with nature; the magistrates hunt them for practising the magic.
our friends be the elementals and they sometimes guide us and we have our secret hideaways
Alchemy, and when the dark side may be called on

Estelle describes alchemists as men groping after powers her people already have, looking under every rock because they dare not ask. She insists some really have made gold — a powder rubbed on lead and heated in a very hot fire — though it reverts a day or two later. Then the rule: the universe must balance, so calling on the dark side selfishly rebounds, but calling on it for someone truly in distress is permitted.
If you call upon the dark side for selfish reasons, then yes, it's a bad thing because it will rebound on you.
Hearing the horses talk

Hiding in the stables, Estelle says she is listening to the horses talking. Anyone can hear the sounds, she explains, but understanding them depends on how much of like mind you are with the mother goddess — with your ears you hear the ordinary noises, inside your head it sounds like two people speaking. The horses gossip about the household and expose the couples who come down believing themselves unobserved.
With your ears, you hear the sounds they normally make. But inside your head, it's like listening to two people talking.
The apprentice, the medicine sapling, and the beginner's initiation

A second subject, years after Karen, emerges into the same order. She stands by a leafless sapling whose twigs are crushed and combined with other potions for the ache and the fevers, knowledge shown to her by the older sisters. She has had only the beginner's initiation, held on the island — the pledge that makes her an apprentice — and says only those already approved are allowed onto the island at all.
The twigs we take and crush them and use what is the product of the crushing in our cures.
part2: Calling down a storm — and losing control of it

Estelle explains why the lord of the manor went mad: he called up a storm to hurl lightning at a neighbouring house, spent his strength summoning it and had nothing left to throw the bolts, so the forces overtook him and left him stranded between worlds. Then the rules — you don't control nature, you work with it inside its natural confines; you can't make rain fall upward; his rituals failed because they were man-centred rather than goddess-centred; a full storm takes about three people.
One night he called down a storm. There are ways and there are ways of calling down rain. And if you do it wrong, it can overtake you and do something strange to you.
Crossroads divination, pentagram and buried coin

The rituals done at a crossroads when you can't decide between two choices: you go at night with a coin, draw symbols in the dust marking which road stands for which choice, bury the coin, wait a set time, then return — and the direction taken by the first person to cross gives the answer. A pentagram always, plus a planetary sign to suit the ritual, Venus for love, drawn with the coin itself.
Usually there's a pentagram and then depending on what kind of a ritual it is would depend on what kind of symbols you put down.
Moon phases mapped onto the seasons

Asked how children are taught which rituals belong to which moon, she gives the mnemonic: new moon is winter, full moon is summer, waxing and waning are spring and fall. Each phase then carries its own class of ritual — increase, fulfillment, finishing off, and cleansing before a new cycle begins.
Rituals for increase and growing you do in the spring or the waxing moon. Rituals of fulfillment and completion you do in summer or the full moon.
Inside names and outside names; the child's first initiation

Everyone in the group carries two names. Outside names are just sounds; inside names hold power that can be used in the rituals, which is why she refuses at first to give her husband's. A child gets an outside name at birth but no inside name until the elders have watched which rituals it does best, around seven, at its primary initiation — where it is questioned, tested on the group rituals, and tested on how well it keeps secrets.
Our inside names contain power in them. Outside names don't really mean anything. They're just sounds.
The egg ritual for preventing pregnancy

Those in harmony with the Earth Mother decide whether and when to have a child. At the midpoint of the cycle you go to the grove at night with hair from your lover's head, your own hair, and an egg; you tell the powers you desire no fruit from the union, smash the egg on the ground as the symbol of nothing coming of it, then turn the focus inward on your own body.
And at this point, you break the egg and smash it on the ground, symbolizing nothing coming of the union.
The pendulum, and witching for water

"I have ways," she says, asked how she knows the unborn child is a girl — then gives the whole method: a pebble, ideally one with a hole, or a coin tied on a thread the length of wrist to inner elbow, held over the outside of the other wrist at a four-finger span. A circle to the right means girl; a circle to the left, or a back-and-forth swing, means boy. Some people simply lack the knack, like those who cannot witch for water.
And if it's a girl, it'll swing in a circle to the right. And if it's a boy, it'll either swing in a circle to the left or just swing back and forth.
The two swans — the story that carries the love ritual

The stories told to children exist to keep complicated ritual gestures in memory, and this is the one behind their love ritual. Swans could once speak; one gossiping swan ruined all swans' reputation, so the swans called a council with the goddess. She agreed to stop the gossip — but something must be given in return to keep everything balanced, so she took their speech and gave them the neck-twining courtship dance instead. Their love rituals imitate those movements with the hands.
And she says, 'I will take your power of speech from you to where you will all be mute.'
Initiation at thirteen, familiars, and scrying for a soulmate

At thirteen a child becomes a full member in a long, heavily symbolic rite and is confirmed in its inside name — unless it has a familiar, in which case the familiar is given an inside name too. Then the soulmate test: on the full moon you take a crystal ball or a black kettle of water outside, stare into the reflective surface thinking of the person, and wait for a confirming sign, different for everyone and unmistakable when it comes.
On the night of the full moon, you get either a crystal ball or a black kettle with some water in it and you go outside in the light of the moon.
The first initiation, and teaching a baby to meditate

The first initiation is simple: a white candle lit, a handful of earth taken up and set before it, a promise to remember you are part of that earth, a symbolic drink of wine, then a celebration. It is done one child at a time, whenever that child is ready, because it needs the meditation they have been taught. Pressed on how you teach a baby, she says it begins before birth — altering the breathing with your mind.
They light a white candle and they take up a handful of earth and put it before it and promise to keep it in mind that they are part of that earth.
The dark side, and the law of rebound

The opening exchange of Part 2. A curse laid for a selfish reason on someone who has done nothing to you will not take hold — it rebounds on the sender, "some say twofold, some say tenfold" — while good sent out simply takes effect and brings back the result you needed. She allows the dark side can be used for good, against cheaters, to set things right. Its opposite isn't "the light side" but the way, or the path.
There's the dark side and the other side is the way or the path because that's the path of which we got our lives.
The secret handfasting in the grove

Estelle nearly married Rough by their own ways the night before but couldn't, because he doesn't know what she is and would have wondered at the rope. The rite: circle the grove, go to the stone at the centre, place an offering on it for the earth mother according to the season, look into each other's eyes and pledge faithfulness before the goddess, then seal it with a rope of flowers the girl has made, laid around them both.
It's best to do it in the waxing of the moon. It should not be done in the dark of the moon. There should be moonlight for it.
Death as a completed cycle, and the funeral rite

The celebration the church most objects to — that they are glad when someone dies, because a cycle has been completed and the next is ready. They grieve missing the person, but not for the soul. Then the funeral rite itself, which they know only by hearsay because the church takes every body: the dead laid within a sacred circle of salt, a pentagram projected upon them, and the tools of whichever rituals they did best arranged around them.
You place them within a sacred circle of salt and you project a pentagram upon them.
What the fairies actually are

Sarah McDonald, the Scottish lacemaker with second sight, says her friends are the fairies and they come and sing for her. Six to nine inches tall, very shy, the females with wings like glitter, the males duller and wingless; not human, not spirit, far older than humans, with an existence that can't be judged by human eyes. She distinguishes them from elves, which are bigger, and gnomes, the hill people said to turn to stone in daylight.
Like the whispering of the wind across the harp strings. They're very soft and very beautiful. It's like music.
What the fairies taught her — finding lost things, plant sprites

Asked whether they taught her bits of magic, she says they taught her to find lost things — by thinking yourself to be the lost thing and asking where you would be. Some fairies live in trees and protect them; water sprites live in wells and springs. Every plant has a protective spirit, and if you acknowledge it and let it know you care about that particular plant, you can ask it to grow.
It's the protective spirit for that plant.
Stones and gems in healing

Alexandro, the Alexandrian physician, is asked whether he treats with colour or with stones. Certain cancers, he says, can be cured with what some men call a lodestone laid over the growth, because its magnetic properties draw the disease out of the body. Pressed on colour he first says he doesn't use it much, then refuses outright — "I'm not at liberty." He confirms crystals are valuable in healing and volunteers nothing more.
It is what some men call a lodestone. It has magnetic properties with which to draw toward it.
Hypnosis as anaesthetic — and the sleep temples

The physician explains his surgical anaesthesia in detail: talk the patient into focusing on your voice, suggest drowsiness, beautiful dreams and no pain, use imagery so their own mind supplies the pictures and they are elsewhere while the body is worked on. It is often easier when the patient is in great pain, because they seize on the promise like a lifeline. He has heard of sleep temples where the troubled were taken, but says that method has been lost.
You use imagery in which their own mind brings up the pictures and it is like they are elsewhere then.
Reading the energy of a limb, and green-light healing

Asked how he tells a break from a sprain, the physician says he runs his hand along the limb and feels the energy — where it does not continue, there is a break — and sets the bone by the same feel, until the flow is complete. Asked whether energy can be increased around a break to speed healing, he describes putting the patient under hypnosis, having them surround the break with a green light and send energy into it from their own body, then planting a trigger word so a family member can repeat it.
I prefer using a green light around that break. And they would do this themselves and send energy from their own body into this.
Recognising one of their own — and what the Inquisition did

Estelle catches the new horse-keeper gesturing to the moon the way they do in honour of the goddess. She doesn't confront him; she tells the elders, and one approaches him obliquely, dropping references only a follower would catch and waiting for the correct responses before anything is said openly — the safeguard against Inquisition infiltrators. It emerges he fled because the Inquisition tortured his pregnant wife to death.
And one evening I caught him gesturing towards the moon similar to the way we do in honor of the goddess.
Sarah McDonald burned for the second sight

Karen drops straight into a traumatic scene: her house is on fire and she does not want to watch. The villagers set it. She was a lacemaker outside Glen Mura in Scotland with second sight; she warned them the crops would fail that year, and when it came to pass they said she had cast an evil eye on the crops and made the sheep lamb too early. The women of her family are all born with the sight.
when I tried to tell them that there would be a problem this year with the crops, and when it came to pass, they said that it was I that cast an evil eye
The mad lord's twisted magic, and the two-headed calf

The broken lord never attacked people — he tried to work twisted magic on them instead, usually failing, occasionally succeeding bizarrely. A friend mentioned his prize cow was in calf; the lord was having a good day and thought he'd help, so he worked a ritual on the cow, and the calf was born with two heads and died. The group has been kept busy keeping all of it under control.
He just tried to work twisted magic on them. Most of the time it would not work. But sometimes it would work in a very bizarre way.
Estelle's murder, and the group's retribution

A disguised inquisitor, having heard of her healing after a child let something slip, comes to her hut, cannot get answers, and tortures and kills her with a heated fire-poker. She narrates the whole thing from above with total detachment — Dolores notes she had the ability to leave her body from years of practice. Her husband calls the group together; two men lure the man into the woods, and they tie him spread-eagled on a large stone. She is sorry her people dirtied themselves with the Inquisition's own tactics.
They went ahead and buried him, and they put some spells over his grave so it would never be found.
The Shee, changelings, and the Beltane fires

O'Keefe the Irish harper calls them "the she" — they dance in the meadows in the moonlight and leave their circles. He explains changelings: the fairies have few children of their own, so they make something in the shape of a child with their magic, leave it and take the real one, and the substitute sickens and dies. He describes people who are pixie magic, who wander off not quite right, and names what the friars call heathen: Beltane, the fires that must always be kept burning.
We call them the she. They dance around in the meadows in the moonlight and leave their circles.
The stone dancers and the coils

O'Keefe doesn't know the word druid, but says the people who raised "the dancers" are gone or in hiding. He has seen the great southern circle himself: stones about man height and blue, leaning at all angles like drunks dancing, with a great black centre altar stone nobody knows the origin of, on which sacrifices are said to have been made. He also describes great coiled mounds of earth in the hills, and says a man who trespasses there tends to disappear.
There's a great center altar stone that they're not sure where it come from. It be black and very dark.
Giza, the inner learning, and the curse of leprosy

Asked where he'd go if he had the choice, the physician names Giza. Alexandria is the centre of the outward learning; Giza is the centre of the inner learning, and his teachers are there. When Dolores presses on whether they live near the pyramids he shuts the subject down flatly. Moments later, asked whether the city's thieves trouble him, he says he simply laid the curse of leprosy on them and they leave him alone.
I just said that I would put the curse of leprosy upon them and they do not bother me.
The Greek oracle — reading smoke, and reading flames

Diane, an initiate at an isolated temple given over to the oracle, describes giving her first reading at 23: you sit with the tripod in front of you, watch the smoke, and tell what you see — students are forbidden to try it before they are judged ready. Later a king comes, and the high priestess uses a different technique: leaves crumbled and tossed into the brazier, read from the way the flames rise and crackle.
You sit there with the tripod in front of you and you watch the smoke and you tell what you see.
